questions.q: How does the Constitution of India guarantee equality to its citizens?
answer: Equality is a core value of Indian democracy, and the Constitution guarantees it as a Fundamental Right.

answer.text: Every person, whether rich or poor, high or low, is equal before the law and entitled to its equal protection.

The Constitution forbids discrimination against any citizen on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth, and gives everyone equal access to public places such as shops, roads and wells.
It abolishes untouchability in any form.
To make equality real, it allows special help — such as reservations and welfare schemes — for disadvantaged groups, so that all can enjoy equal opportunity.

questions.q: Why does inequality persist despite legal guarantees, and how can society become more equal?
answer: Although the law promises equality, real inequalities continue in Indian society.

answer.text: People still face unequal treatment because of caste, religion, gender, disability and poverty. Such discrimination denies people their dignity, the right to be treated with respect.
Laws can forbid discrimination, but they cannot by themselves change deep-rooted attitudes and social customs, which is why inequality survives.

Government steps such as free education, healthcare and the midday meal scheme widen opportunity, but lasting change also needs a shift in people's attitudes so that everyone is treated as an equal in daily life.

questions.q: What is equality, and why is it important in a democracy?

answer.text: Equality means that all human beings are of equal worth and should be treated in the same way, with the same rights and the same respect, regardless of their religion, caste, sex, wealth or the language they speak.

answer.lead: Why it matters in a democracy.
answer.text: Equality is one of the foundations of democracy. In a democracy every citizen, rich or poor, has one vote of equal value and an equal say in choosing the government. All are equal before the law, and no one may be treated as superior or inferior by birth.
True equality also means giving everyone a fair chance, so that people held back for long, such as the poor or the discriminated, get special help to catch up.

answer: Thus equality means equal worth and equal treatment, and it is essential for a fair and truly democratic society.

questions.q: How do dignity and self-respect relate to equality? Illustrate with examples.

answer.text: Real equality is not only about laws but about treating every person with dignity and self-respect. When people are looked down upon or humiliated because of their caste, poverty or work, their dignity is denied, and they are not truly equal.

The practice of untouchability, by which some people were treated as impure and kept apart, was a cruel denial of dignity. Poor people are sometimes made to feel small or are refused entry to certain places, which too hurts their self-respect.
The Constitution abolished untouchability and guarantees equal respect to all. Schemes like the common midday meal, where all children eat together, help break such barriers and uphold dignity.

answer: Thus equality is meaningful only when every person is treated with dignity and self-respect.
